atAGlance: Tôm chiên xù is breaded fried shrimp with a golden crisp coating and sweet shrimp inside, often shared as a snack or seafood starter.
whatItIs: Tôm chiên xù is breaded fried shrimp, usually crisp outside with tender shrimp inside, served with lime, salt, chili, or a mayonnaise-style dip depending on the shop.
usuallyIncludes: chili or mayo-style dip if served
howToEnjoy: Eat while the coating is crisp, and check whether tails or shells remain. Dip lightly so the breading stays crunchy.
howLocalsOrder: Order tôm chiên xù when you want crunchy fried shrimp. Ask about shells, no chili, or extra lime-pepper salt before sharing.
worthKnowing: Chiên xù signals a crumbed, crunchy fried style, useful for recognizing shrimp, fish, or pork cutlet dishes.
goodToKnow: Eat it hot so the coating stays crisp. Ask whether the shrimp are peeled if you prefer an easier bite.
travelerCaution: Contains or may contain seafood or shellfish.
